rules.when: The task is a trivial mechanical edit such as a rote rename, formatting sweep, targeted typo fix, or simple file gathering.
rules.why: Cheapest fast profile for narrow, low-ambiguity work.

rules.when: The task is ordinary feature or bug-fix work of moderate scope and ambiguity - the common everyday case.
rules.why: Sonnet 5 at medium effort is the balanced tier for routine coding.

rules.when: The task is a big or ambiguous multi-file feature, a risky refactor, or work that requires holding many moving parts in mind.
rules.why: Strongest profile for broad design and implementation work.

rules.when: The task designs something other agents will use or read: agent-facing knowledge structures and conventions (e.g. an AGENTS.md guide, a knowledge base layout, entry templates and schemas agents parse), skills, agent instructions or prompts, or tooling and interfaces whose main consumers are agents.
rules.why: Captain standing policy (2026-11-08): design decisions consumed by other agents compound across every later session, so they get the strongest profile.
